title: Chapter 42: Steamed Potatoes
content:
Chapter 42:

Steamed Potatoes

Far away, his consciousness drifted among the waves.

Shimmering ripples, amidst a slumber, his consciousness repeatedly bobbed up and down in the boundary between dream and reality.

“—is there any other way to—”

“—I suppose. The rest is up to you, in fact.”

Far away—no, close by—on the border between here and there, he could hear the voices of people arguing.

A voice clinging, a voice pushing away, a tearful voice, a voice with frozen emotions. Voices.

Suddenly, a soft sensation enveloped his palm.

He was reminded that it was the feeling of someone’s hand, drawn from memories of having touched it several times before.

He was sure he had felt this warmth like this before.

However, the sensation of that palm suddenly grew distant.

Leaving his hand, far, far away, so high up it couldn’t be touched, higher and higher.

And then,

“—will definitely save you.”

Only that strong determination remained, leaving him behind.

Everything was disappearing, leaving him behind, going away. Far, far away.

And then—

※※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※

Having his consciousness forcibly shut down and waking up like this—how many times had he experienced this now?

Staring at the unfamiliar patterns on the ceiling, Subaru thought this vaguely.

There was this way old pillow talk cliché that it’d be over by the time you finish counting the stains on the ceiling, but given the number of stains at the cultural level of this other world, it’d be quite a long haul—he smiled wryly at such pointless thoughts, only for his side to cramp, causing an involuntary groan to escape his lips.

“Oof, ow…”

Trying to touch his aching side, an explosive sense of wrongness shot through his left arm as he moved it. Following that sensation, he brought his left hand in front of his face, and upon seeing its sorry state, he understood why.

From the fingertips of his left arm down to his wrist, raised white scars densely covered his skin. Furthermore, those wounds were stitched together with some sort of warped, clumsy thread; if someone told him a kid who sucked at sewing had haphazardly stitched it up, he would have believed it.

That wasn’t the only place that felt wrong.

Rolling up the hem of his shirt, he found similar stitching on his cramping right flank. On top of that, both his ankles, around the bicep of his right arm, around his right shoulder, and even his ass—the list went on. Every single one of them bore scars and stitches, enough to make him feel a bit like a cyborg.

As he stroked the various parts of his completely altered body to check on them, his memories slowly began to return alongside a faint pain.

Right, he had gone deep into the forest to search for the kids, encountered the witchbeasts, and—

“I totally thought I was dead, though…”

He had shielded Rem from that attack and bathed his entire body in the witchbeasts’ fangs.

The ferocious beasts’ jaws should have easily crunched through Subaru’s flesh, tearing him apart and shredding him like scrap paper. He had clearly felt his life spilling away, and had been half-convinced it was all over.

“I wouldn’t call myself a mummy… Seeing how much I’ve been mended with a needle and thread, I guess a Jiangshi is a more accurate image.”

Or, if they’d slammed a bolt into his head, maybe Frankenstein’s monster.

Reaching that point in his thoughts, he suddenly realized his own carefreeness.

“—Right. This is no time for stupid jokes. What about Rem and the kids?”

Springing up from the simple bed, Subaru looked around to grasp the situation.

An unfamiliar ceiling, a crude bed. A cramped room with shabby furniture; he couldn’t possibly imagine this being Roswaal Manor.

And then, right by the entrance—he noticed the presence of a silver-haired girl sitting on a wooden chair, her head bowed in sleep.

“Emilia-tan.”

There was no sign of her responding to his call.

Her dozing slumber seemed deep; the steady rhythm of her breathing was quite profound. Unusually, her beautiful silver hair was slightly disheveled, as if she hadn’t even had the time to tidy it. More than anything, he could see terrible stains of blood and mud lingering all over her clothes.

His injured self. Greeting the morning in a bed. Emilia sleeping in a chair right beside him. And her clothes dirtied with blood and the like.

Considering those points, even someone as dense as Subaru could figure out the situation.

In short,

“I ended up owing Emilia-tan another debt, huh…”

“I wonder about that. I do think you should be at least somewhat grateful to Lia, but this time around, I think there’s someone else you should be thanking a lot more.”

Responding to Subaru’s self-reproaching murmur was the gray cat, making an appearance from within the silver hair.

He lightly stroked the sleeping Emilia’s cheek with a paw pad, then floated over to hover right in front of Subaru’s face.

“Yo, good morning. How are you feeling after waking up?”

“It’s hard to say I’m in tip-top shape. I’ve become a cyborg before I even knew it. Makes me want to escape before they mess with my brain and I play the masked hero who takes revenge on the evil 

syndicate.”

1

“Cyborg… ah, you mean the threads. It couldn’t be helped. Your body’s internal mana simply wasn’t enough to heal you normally. We had to rely on tools just to stitch you back together. If we hadn’t, you’d probably be in pieces right now, you know?”

“That’s a terrifying thought! Even so, couldn’t someone a little better at sewing have done it?”

Even if he didn’t mind the sutures themselves, he wanted to file a complaint about the poor workmanship. Especially as someone who boasted an S-rank in sewing skills, he felt the urge to drill the basics into whoever did this.

At Subaru’s words, Puck waved his hands dismissively, saying “No, no.”

“It’s been a long time since I ran a needle through a human body. I ended up putting too much force into it here and there; it was pretty tough.”

“Of all people, it was you?! Actually, how did you even manage to sew with that tiny body of yours?!”

“You weren’t moving, so it was easy. The bleeding was terrible, so there were a lot of spots where I had to freeze the wounds while doing it, so you’ll just have to bear with that.”

“So that’s why my scars are weirdly white… Well, I’m a guy, so I’m not gonna whine about scars being left behind or anything.”

Looking over the various scars, Subaru then turned to face Puck once more.

Puck looked blankly at Subaru’s sudden shift in posture, but to the black-eyed spirit, Subaru bowed his head deeply.

“Thanks to you, I survived. Thank you. I picked up my life again.”

“Yep, yep, being honest is a good thing. Besides, you did your fair share this time around too. It would have been far too pitiful if you’d just collapsed and died after all that. So it’s totally fine.”

Puck replied without any embarrassment to Subaru’s words of gratitude. Having the weight lifted from his chest by those words, Subaru prefaced with “In that case,” and asked,

“Hearing I did my fair share makes me happy, but… what actually happened after that? Honestly, I don’t remember anything past the point where I was getting chomped on by those dogs in the forest.”

“‘Chomped on’ is a rather cute way of putting it. Judging by your condition when you were brought in, I thought it was more of a 

munch-crunch-squelch-rip-tear-splat

 kind of situation.”

“Hey, hey, with sound effects like that, I’m definitely dead. That’s a ‘missing five or six arms’ type of pattern; one of me wouldn’t be enough.”

“Yeah, which is why, well, that blue-haired maid girl was also in a pretty terrible state.”

Hearing it said so lightly and casually, Subaru’s throat involuntarily froze. In response to Subaru’s reaction, Puck added “Although,” before continuing.

“In her case, the wounds healed rapidly due to the effects of her Oni transformation. By the time she carried you back to the village, there were no noticeable external injuries. She didn’t even need healing magic.”

“Don’t scare me for nothing… Anyway, Rem made it back to the village too, huh. And what about the other one, the kid who was carried back with me?”

“She was there, so you can rest easy. The six children, plus one more makes seven. And then there’s you; it’s a good thing that blue-haired girl is so strong. In the end, your decision was absolutely correct.”

“Clap, clap,” Puck said aloud while bringing his hands together in a silent clap. The softness of his paw pads got in the way, preventing any actual clapping sound. Subaru’s lips almost curled into a smile at the heartwarming sight, but he shook his head to banish the thought.

“Puck, I’ve got a few things I want to ask you, is that alright?”

“As long as you keep your voice down so Lia doesn’t wake up. My manifestation right now is powered by the mana I stored up overnight, but when I was out during the middle of the night, I was using Lia’s Od.”

“Od?”

“Mana is what you take in from the outside world. In contrast, Od is something originally inherent within a living creature’s body; it’s literally the power of the soul. Unlike mana, using Od chips away at one’s own life force, so I don’t really want her using it much.”

As he spoke, Puck directed his gaze toward Emilia, looking at her as if she was his troubled daughter.

Drawn in, Subaru stared at her sleeping face, easily accepting Puck’s explanation. If it came to Emilia, she wouldn’t hesitate if she needed to sacrifice her own life force to save someone. If she needed Puck last night and the price was her own self, he could easily imagine she wouldn’t have had a shred of hesitation in her decision.

“Does that mean I was saved at the cost of Emilia-tan sacrificing her own life force?”

“That’s part of it. But in yesterday’s case, my role was mainly for the children—the kids you brought back from the forest. My objective was to lift their curses.”

“The curses… Right! There was that too. Are the kids gonna be alright? What about the curses?”

“You can relax about that, too.”

Stopping Subaru, who looked ready to press him for details, with a paw, Puck twisted his feline face into an adorable smile.

“The healing magic kept their debilitation largely in check, and the curse-lifting went smoothly, so there’s no problem. I definitely lifted the curses on the children.”

Puck thumped his chest as if giving his seal of approval. Seeing this, Subaru let out a deep breath, relieved by the fact that his actions hadn’t ended up being meaningless.

And, as the human body is a fickle opportunist once peace of mind sets in,

“Oh.”

Right after a sense of relief dominated his heart, the bug in Subaru’s stomach let out a loud, screaming growl.

Touching his stomach, feeling something akin to pain in its emptiness, he remembered that he had missed out on dinner last night.

“By the way, as long as I absorb mana, I don’t get hungry.”

“I didn’t ask. But still, since mana is everywhere, getting full just by breathing air makes you sound like a plant.”

“I don’t need water or sunlight either. All I need is love. When associating with a spirit, that’s an important thing you must never forget.”

“Yeah, yeah. Is it alright if I go outside to take a look?”

When he pointed at the door and asked, Puck crossed his arms and nodded a few times.

“I think that’s fine. It’s better if you move around a bit and get a feel for your patchwork state. Oh, and the threads will be absorbed into your body and disappear on their own once they’ve settled in.”

“Oh, good. It’d be way too hard to try and pass off these stitches that look like squirming earthworms as high fashion. Like I was born about two hundred light-years too early or something.”

In response to his full-force gag, Puck just tilted his head with a smile.

It seemed it didn’t land. The plan had been a golden comedic routine: getting a straight-man retort like “Light-years measure distance,” and then following up with “That’s how alien the fashion sense is.”

With Puck’s permission, Subaru headed out of the room.

On his way, he gave a small bow to Emilia, who was sleeping right next to the door. As he bowed, her sleeping face caught his eye; breathing heavily at the sight of her peaceful slumber, he was filled with the urge to pull a prank on her, but the strict glare of her guardian right nearby made him give up. Resigning himself, he stepped outside.

And then,

“Ah, well, I guess it makes perfect sense.”

Stepping out of the room and poking his head outside the building through the entryway right in front of him, Subaru muttered that upon seeing the village in an uproar.

The time was just shortly after the morning sun had begun to rise, but a large number of figures had already gathered in the plaza at the center of the village.

It was a small village. The number of people there constituted pretty much the entire population. The elderly, women, and children huddled together, looking anxious, while a group centered around robust youths surrounded them defensively.

The ones surrounding and protecting the villagers were the youth group who had put all their efforts into searching for the children the previous night. Within their encirclement, Subaru couldn’t find the faces he was looking for. Tilting his head, he turned his steps toward another building where people were frequently going in and out.

But before that,

“—Barusu, you’re awake.”

Called out to from behind, Subaru stopped and turned around.

Although the nickname immediately gave away who it was, seeing her face in person made a feeling of relief naturally win out within him.

Standing behind him was the pink-haired maid—Ram.

She had the sleeves of her familiar uniform rolled up, and in her hands, she was carrying something like a colander piled high with what looked like steamed potatoes.

A faint, salty aroma drifted from the slightly steaming potatoes, causing Subaru’s empty stomach to cheer with anticipation and excitement.

As Subaru’s stomach let out a sound similar to the onomatopoeia Puck had used earlier, Ram snorted with a “Hmph,” and said,

“Causing such a worry with those severe injuries, only to shamelessly demand food the moment you wake up. Were you bitten by a dog and ended up catching ‘dog’?”

“Setting aside my ‘what exactly does catching dog mean’ retort—hmm, I see, really now, so you 

were

 worried about me?”

Stretching his back, leaning in, and swaying from side to side, he stepped closer to Ram with a smug look on his face.

Ram narrowed her eyes at Subaru’s teasing attitude.

“Eat this.”

“Mmrph!”

A steamed potato was forcefully shoved into his mouth, literally crushing his words in his throat.

To make matters worse, a searing heat ravaged the inside of his mouth. Subaru looked up, panting roughly like an animal, “Hahf! Hahf!” Then,

“I thought I was gonna die! It was delicious though!”

“It was delicious, wasn’t it. It’s freshly baked… no, freshly steamed.”

“What’s with that smug look, it’s pissing me off! It was delicious though!”

“Yes, yes. Ram’ll give you another one, so just shut up and gorge yourself.”

Handed another potato, he accepted it, cheering like a kid. Ram looked at Subaru with contempt for a moment, then said,

“Well, regarding last night’s incident, Ram’ll honestly give you my thanks. Good work.”

“Saying ‘good work’ makes you sound incredibly condescending, you know. Well, whatever… but is this really something 

you

 need to thank me for?”

“If any harm comes to the people of this domain, the responsibility falls on the Lord. When I think about what would have happened if those children had been left at the mercy of that pack of ulgarms… Barusu’s actions were the correct ones.”

“Ulgarms,

2

 huh…”

That must’ve been the name of those black witchbeasts.

Quite an imposing name they’d been given. Just hearing it once was enough to convey that they were the kind of existence that threatened your life simply by encountering them.

At Subaru’s nod, Ram turned her gaze toward the forest.

“Last night, Ram re-tied the barrier that had apparently come undone. After that, she spent the whole night patrolling to see if there were any issues with the barrier, so there shouldn’t be any witchbeasts slipping through to this side.”

“As long as nobody slips through from 

this

 side, right? If those brats cross the barrier, go to the other side, and bring a baby back with them, it defeats the whole purpose.”

“That hurts to hear. Ever since the barrier was set up around the area, there hasn’t even been a minor skirmish with witchbeasts, so we’d let our guard down. —Ram’ll give them a stern talking-to.”

The fact that her wording wasn’t exactly gentle was likely because she had her own reasons to be irritated. For Subaru, it was the displeasure of getting dragged into this mess, but for her, it was probably directed at the villagers who hadn’t properly listened to Roswaal’s instructions.

Thinking of her extreme loyalty, he couldn’t help but pity the villagers who were about to be lectured.

While pressing his hands together in prayer for the pitiable villagers in his heart, Subaru suddenly felt a bout of dizziness.

His body staggered involuntarily, and as he held his head, Ram lightly supported him with her hand.

“Don’t push yourself. Truly, had the Great Spirit and Lady Beatrice not been here, those were wounds you absolutely should have died from.”

“Hearing Beako’s name means I owe her one too… What a blunder!”

“Even if it was at the Great Spirit’s request, it’s rare for Lady Beatrice to leave the Forbidden Library, let alone step outside the mansion. She is someone who cannot utilize her full power outside the mansion, however.”

Regaining his balance with the support of Ram’s hand, Subaru gave his head a light shake.

It really felt like he was lacking blood. There was a lethargy similar to his first morning at Roswaal Manor, and the heaviness in the tips of his limbs was probably due to a severe mana deficiency. According to Puck, they had stitched together some rather catastrophic injuries.

With Subaru’s inherently low mana reserves, it wouldn’t be strange if he was completely drained.

“Ram will watch over the village’s progress a little longer before returning to the mansion. She is concerned about the condition of the children whose curses were lifted, as well… and regarding countermeasures against the ulgarms.”

“When you say countermeasures, isn’t it okay to just have the barrier up?”

“If this were like the minor skirmishes we’ve had until now, perhaps that would have been fine.”

Ram responded to Subaru’s modest question with her usual emotionless face.

However, being stared back at by those supposedly emotionless eyes, Subaru couldn’t stop goosebumps from breaking out over his spine, as if a spike of ice had been driven down it.

To Subaru, she spoke each word slowly, as if chewing on them to extract their full meaning.

“Causing harm to the village, and on top of that, doing this much damage to Barusu, an affiliate of Master Roswaal’s mansion—there is absolutely no way we will let this go unaddressed.”

“Wh-What do you intend to do…?”

As Subaru inadvertently slipped into formal speech, Ram suddenly erased that intimidating aura, lightly running her fingers through her pink hair.

“Ram will wipe them out. —Though, that will be after Master Roswaal returns. Once Master Roswaal is back, it won’t be a matter that takes much time at all.”

Given the absolute trust placed in those words, there was no room for Subaru to argue.

Even without knowing the full extent of Roswaal’s capabilities, he could deeply understand the sheer magnitude of Ram’s trust in him.

After that, Subaru robbed Ram of about two more steamed potatoes before they parted ways.

After parting, she headed toward the group of villagers who were still huddled together, looking anxious. It was likely her own way of showing consideration. The fact that her chosen method of expressing that consideration was steamed potatoes just perfectly captured Ram’s unrefined atmosphere.

“But these steamed potatoes are amazing. Seriously, the saltiness is just too perfect.”

Nibbling on the received steamed potatoes, Subaru continued to stroll around the village.

While checking the condition of his body, he simultaneously went around confirming the safety of the children they had recovered from the forest. The children themselves were still fast asleep due to the exhaustion from the previous night and the mana depletion from having their curses lifted, but he received an overwhelming amount of gratitude from their parents.

Honestly, Subaru, who hadn’t done it for the sake of being thanked, panicked to death. Completely flustered beyond belief, he ended up choosing to flee out of sheer embarrassment without even managing to crack a decent joke.

Breaking into a cold sweat at their unexpected welcome, Subaru judged he had accomplished his main objectives. Planning to return to the room where he’d been sleeping and wait for Emilia to wake up, he suddenly realized he still hadn’t seen the blue-haired girl.

—Suddenly, the image of a demon bathed in blood spatter, roaring with laughter, flashed across his mind.

In that instant, he didn’t think it was an emotion like fear that made his body tremble.

It was something more overwhelming, a hard-to-describe emotion akin to standing before a higher existence that one had to look up to as a living creature. Or perhaps, that was what people called awe.

With a white horn growing from her forehead, burying witchbeasts using inhuman strength, that figure was exactly the very image of the demons passed down in legends.

He felt anxious about whether he could act the same way as always when standing before her.

“No, no, I was perfectly fine with her twin, Ram, so what am I even worrying about? If Rem is a demon, then Ram’s a demon too… Haven’t I been having some incredibly rare experiences here?!”

Making himself forget his own cowardice with a flippant remark, Subaru shook his head to refresh his memories.

He was feeling this way because he kept recalling only the most shocking scenes from last night. He needed to think of a more brilliant sight, one filled with enough exhilaration to make him forget those gruesome scenes—.

The scene of her iron ball crushing a witchbeast’s head, blowing away its torso, and smashing through the pack floated into his mind.

“Wait, even if I leave out the part where she turned into a demon, I can still only picture pure splatter. And, ugh, just remembering it is making me sick…”

The feast of blood and viscera suddenly came back to him, and Subaru pressed a hand over his mouth as a wave of nausea hit.

Swaying unsteadily, he headed toward the edge of the building, crouched in the tall grass, and breathed heavily. It seemed he’d somehow manage to hold it in, and he breathed a sigh of relief.

After all, these were the steamed potatoes he’d finally shoved into his empty stomach. Not to mention, they were a precious item packed with Ram’s own unique brand of consideration. His reputation as a man would be ruined if he let them go to waste.

Having narrowly held back his vomit, Subaru praised himself and nodded vigorously.

Then, he raised his head, determined to face Rem anew, and—

“—You’re in just the right place, I suppose.”

From beyond the grass, the girl with cream-colored hair in vertical twin drills made her appearance. Catching sight of Subaru, she beckoned to him,

“I have something to discuss with you, I suppose. Come along for a b— “

Bleeaaaarghhh

””

Overlapping the tail end of Beatrice’s haughty words, everything he had thought he’d held back came pouring out.

“KYAAAAAAAAAA!!”

She actually lets out a surprisingly cute scream, huh,

 Subaru thought, as he continued to violently throw up the potatoes, unable to stop once the floodgates had opened.

White, very white, steamed potatoes continued to be expelled without end.

※※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※

Once the commotion had died down, Subaru was led by Beatrice to the back of a building right next to the witchbeast forest.

Previously, this area had been lined with small, independent shops, but naturally, on the morning following a witchbeast disturbance, there wasn’t a single villager aimlessly wandering about.

This current location, lined with completely deserted houses, was indeed the perfect spot for a secret conversation within the village.

“So, what exactly is your business, calling me out to a place like this?”

“That’s hardly the attitude of someone who was puking his guts out until just a moment ago, I suppose. You should reflect on your actions, I suppose.”

“Ah, thanks for rubbing my back, I feel a little better. Oh, by the way, I heard you helped stitch my body back together, too.”

“When you show the exact same level of gratitude for the former and the latter, it leaves Betty at a slight loss as to how to interact with you, I suppose.”

Either way, he was genuinely thankful, so he wanted her to just honestly accept it.

Setting aside Subaru’s thoughts, Beatrice was acting quite unlike her usual self, her gaze darting around incessantly as she fiddled with the hem of her skirt with her fingers in bewilderment.

Her demeanor suggested she had something difficult to talk about.

He thought it was an uncharacteristic attitude for her, who was usually quite frank and spoke her mind to Subaru. Or perhaps it was also influenced by the fact that her expression seemed fitting for her apparent age—giving off the vibe of ‘a child afraid of being scolded by her parents.’

With her making a face like that, Subaru couldn’t exactly aggressively press her to continue. Crossing his arms and leaning his back against the building, Subaru decided to wait for her words.

However, he didn’t need to maintain that waiting stance for very long.

The fact that Subaru didn’t rush her seemed to have conversely spurred her resolve.

Beatrice closed her eyes, then forced them open as if she had steeled herself.

And then,

“Bubby has his own reasons for it, I suppose. But keeping quiet about this wouldn’t be fair to you, I suppose.”

“Bubby,” the term of endearment she used, could only refer to Puck.

Recalling the little gray cat he had just spoken with a short while ago, Subaru tilted his head at her phrasing, making his confusion clear.

To that Subaru, Beatrice said,

“Bubby favors that mixed-blood girl, so he prioritizes her. That’s the correct thing to do as a spirit, I suppose. But as for Betty, I am dissatisfied, I suppose.”

“What are you…”

…trying to say

, were the words Subaru was unable to continue.

Before he could, Beatrice opened her mouth, speaking over him.

She declared.

“—In less than half a day, you are going to die, I suppose.”
